topNeeds.text: Automate satellite hotspot detection (e.g., NGFS) and embed AI safety nets into AWIPS to prevent missed ignitions and reduce forecaster cognitive overload.
Deliver automated push alerts and user-defined geographic watchboxes to dispatchers and analysts, replacing continuous manual dashboard monitoring.
Expose robust APIs to stream satellite thermal detections and smoke model guidance directly into common operating platforms like AWIPS and DESI.
Overlay satellite detections with base weather, fuel moisture, and topographic layers to validate thermal anomalies and eliminate false positives.
Provide high-resolution geolocation and rapid 5-minute data cadences to verify initial wildfire activity across jurisdictional and tribal borders.
Systematically incorporate partner-provided ground-truth fuel moisture data into warning workflows prior to Red Flag Warning issuance.
Issue 48-hour early planning signals and explicit multi-day duration details in Red Flag Warnings to support proactive resource scaling.
Integrate combined text-and-graphic probabilistic visual summaries into core warning products to replace static binary forecasts.
Prioritize forecast stability for core wind and relative humidity variables while generating rapidly-refreshing ensemble smoke guidance in AQI units.
Expand deliberate use of Forecast Discussions during critical periods to explicitly detail forecaster confidence, rationale, and upcoming risk trends.
Establish direct interactive digital chat and SMS notification loops between forecasters and field crews for real-time situational awareness.
Transition tactical Fire Warnings to Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA) to deliver geofenced mobile alerts during life-threatening, rapid-onset incidents.
Implement direct notification pathways with confirmation loops so forecasters know land managers received time-sensitive hotspot alerts.
Implement 'Particularly Dangerous Situation' (PDS) headers during extreme Red Flag Warning events to distinguish catastrophic risk from routine alerts.
Deploy graphical warning software (e.g., Hazard Services) to draw threat polygons with buffer zones instead of broad county-wide warnings.
Institutionalize Tactical IWT frameworks, clarify multi-agency decision authority lines, align with ICS, and embed procedures into state Annual Operating Plans (AOPs).
Conduct joint pre-season interagency training and operational simulations to establish trusted relationships and procedures before active incidents occur.
Dedicate forecaster staffing hours for routine, pre-season partner consultations to align weather products with end-user operational workflows.
Establish adaptable implementation guidelines that allow local NWS offices and public safety agencies to customize warning workflows based on regional risk.
Formalize government-to-government data-sharing agreements, honor Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK), and co-produce risk outreach materials.
